repo.name: pycparser
repo.description: :snake: Complete C99 parser in pure Python

readme.summary: Well-structured documentation with excellent clarity and context but lacks inline quick-start examples, requiring users to navigate to separate files.
readme.top_issue: No inline quick-start code example showing basic parsing usage - users must browse the examples directory to see actual code

injection_risks.description: The use of subprocess.check_output with user-provided input (cpp_path and cpp_args) poses a risk of command injection.
The use of Template.substitute may pose a risk of template injection, but it appears to be used with trusted input.

critical_findings: Command injection risk due to the use of subprocess.check_output with user-provided input
security.summary: The pycparser package has some security concerns, including a high-risk command injection vulnerability and potential issues with input validation and error exposure.

common_complaints: Breaking changes in v3.0.0 affecting downstream projects (cx_Freeze)
Abandoned dependency (PLY library) bundled and outdated since 2017
Parser limitations with C standard features (empty case statements, string concatenation, compound literals)
AST ambiguity issues in named initializers
praise_themes: Major refactoring effort to remove PLY dependency
sentiment.summary: pycparser shows moderate maintenance with a major v3.0.0 refactoring in progress, but community frustration is rising due to breaking changes, reliance on abandoned dependencies (PLY), and unresolved parser limitations for valid C code.

communication.summary: The maintainer provides generally helpful and technically deep responses, but could improve in terms of clarity, patience, and welcomingness towards new contributors.
